title: 前 Avalanche Studios 负责人 Natalie Francis 加入 Massive Entertainment 出任总经理
content:
Avalanche chief joins Massive Entertainment as managing director
Business
News
Former Avalanche Studios chief Natalie Francis joins Massive Entertainment as managing director
Francis will step into the role starting October 1st following Thomas Andren's recent appoint as general manager for the creative network.
Diego Argüello
,
Contributing Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 24, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image via Massive Entertainment
Natalie Francis, former head of studio operations and development at DICE and chief development officer at Avalanche Studios, is joining Massive Entertainment on October 1st.
As
announced
by the studio, Francis will be the new managing director of the Ubisoft subsidiary, which has worked on the likes of
Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora
and
Star Wars Outlaws
in recent times.
"Massive Entertainment has an extraordinary history, built by incredibly talented people and a culture that cares deeply about craft and quality," Francis says in the announcement. "I'm excited to build on that foundation and help create the conditions for the studio and its people to thrive in its next chapter."
Meanwhile, Christoph Hartmann, general manager for Creative House 2—one of the
structural subdivisions within Ubisoft
after its restructuring earlier this year—speaks about Francis' longstanding legacy and translating those skills to her new role.
Related:

"Natalie's extensive experience bringing talented, multidisciplinary teams together around a clear creative and business vision makes her ideally suited to lead Massive into its next chapter. Her track record of delivering ambitious player experiences while connecting long-term strategy with operational excellence provides a strong foundation for the studio and its talented teams moving forward."
Massive Entertainment has had a rocky 2026, which can be said for most of Ubisoft subsidiaries. In October 2025, the parent company announced yet another staff reduction across its global network of studios, specifically around Massive, taking
the form of a voluntary buyout
. At the time, Ubisoft referred to it as a "voluntary career transition program." Those who took the buyout were set to receive a "comprehensive package" that included "financial and career assistance."
Then, in January of this year, the parent company confirmed that it
intended to make 55 people redundant
at both Massive Entertainment and Ubisoft Stockholm, with the proposed restructure following the completion of the aforementioned voluntary redundancy program. Other staff members across
San Francisco
,
Winnipeg and Belgrade
, and
Barcelona
were also affected by their own series of job cuts throughout the year.
Massive Entertainment is currently leading the development of
Tom Clancy's The Division 2
and the forthcoming
Tom Clancy's The Division 3
.
